device: H3C Magic RT3000 (Machine B), running R1-NET-D on mtd16
severity_policy: Assigned by USER IMPACT, not technical complexity.

severity_definitions.P0: Cannot be used as a router normally / data corruption / security or device risk / crash, reboot or OOM / core networking unavailable
severity_definitions.P1: Major function missing (LAN/WAN/Wi-Fi/NSS) / serious performance or stability problem
severity_definitions.P2: LED / UI / default config / log noise / optional tracing / polish

summary.note: RT3-B002 and RT3-B018 CLOSED by the network bring-up (R1-NET-D / R1-NET-B). RT3-RB001 and RT3-RB002 are the remaining P0 release blockers for Product R1.

bugs.title: Packaged rt3bcwrite --set lacks per-copy sequential verify gate
bugs.impact: The packaged selector writer processes both BOOTCONFIG copies in a single invocation and does not enforce the independent mtd3 write -> verify -> mtd2 write -> verify safety gate. A failure between copies can leave the pair in an unverified mixed state without an intervening check.
evidence: rt3bcwrite.c main(): after the disagreement check it runs write_selector(&B) for mtd3 then write_selector(&A) for mtd2 with no intermediate verify gate
Observed live during the authorized slot flip: the packaged tool updates both copies in one call
The strict per-copy ordering was achieved only by building a separate single-copy tool (rt3sel1.c) whose write path is byte-identical to the proven writer
bugs.suggested_fix_area: rt3bcwrite --set to perform and report a verify after each copy, failing closed before touching the second
bugs.note: Registered per R1_FIX_PROBE_A instruction. BOOTCONFIG internals were NOT re-researched and the selector was NOT touched.
bugs.fix: per-copy fail-closed transaction in package/rt3bcwrite.c; tests/rb001 22 assertions

hardware_acceptance.ordering_proven: mtd3 write=PASS verify=PASS emitted before mtd2 SECOND

bugs.title: Both Wi-Fi radios ship disabled - no wireless at all
bugs.impact: The device provides no wireless service of any kind. As a consumer router this is a primary function.
evidence: wireless.radio0.disabled='1' and wireless.radio1.disabled='1' in /etc/config/wireless
wifi status: radio0 up=false disabled=true; radio1 up=false disabled=true
wlan0 and wlan1 operstate=down, txpower 0.00 dBm
bugs.root_cause: Shipped default configuration decision at image build time. NOT a driver, firmware, BDF, caldata or regulatory failure - all of those measured healthy (both phys report 'qmi caldata downloaded: type: 2').
bugs.not_a_bug_note: Determined to be default-config, not firstboot behaviour: /etc/config/wireless exists in the image fully populated with AP interfaces.

probe_a_findings.method: non-persistent UCI enable + ephemeral PSK, then reverted
probe_a_findings.wlan0: type AP, ssid RT3-PROBE-2G, ch1 2412MHz 20MHz, txpower 25.00 dBm, beaconing
probe_a_findings.wlan1: type AP, ssid RT3-PROBE-5G, ch36 5180MHz 80MHz, txpower 24.00 dBm, beaconing
probe_a_findings.hostapd: running with sockets for wlan0 and wlan1
probe_a_findings.nss: Created a NSS virtual interface for both wlan0 and wlan1
probe_a_findings.conclusion: Both radios are fully functional; the P0 was purely the shipped disabled='1' default. FIX PROVEN by runtime.

bugs.title: WAN RX datapath dead - link and TX work, zero frames ever received
bugs.impact: No internet connectivity. The device cannot route traffic upstream, so it is not functioning as a router.
evidence: ubus network.interface.wan status -> up=false, pending=true, proto=dhcp, device=eth0, data={}
ip route show -> only '192.0.2.0/24 dev br-lan scope link src 192.0.2.1'; no default route
logread: repeated 'wan (1341): udhcpc: sending discover' with no offer
eth0 link up with carrier 1 but no IPv4 address
bugs.root_cause: QSDK 11.5 never enables gephy_gcc_tx, the P_GEPHY_TX parent of gmac0_rx/tx_clk_src. Both RCGs therefore fall back to their reset parent xo (24 MHz). Root cause: the gate at src/adpt/mp/adpt_mp_portctrl.c:919 'if (uniphy_mode_new != uniphy_mode_old)' is FALSE because mac_mode was already seeded to 0xf from the DT switch_mac_mode (R1 boot log: 'mac mode = 0xf'). adpt_mp_uniphy_mode_configure() - the ONLY code that sets UNIPHY_CLK_RATE_125M via ssdk_mp_raw_clock_set() - is skipped. gephy_gcc_tx stays enable_count=0 and the RCGs sit on xo. 24 MHz cannot sample a 1000BASE-T stream, so every received frame fails CRC.
bugs.caveat: 1000BASE-T initial bring-up qualified. Physical 1G unplug/replug (NET-QUAL-001), 100BASE-T (NET-QUAL-002) and 10BASE-T (NET-QUAL-003) remain untested and must NOT be recorded as PASS.

probe_a_findings.subnet_conflict_handling: upstream 192.0.2.0/24 overlapped product LAN; LAN moved NON-PERSISTENTLY to 192.168.50.1/24 to test; overlap NOT treated as a firmware fault
probe_a_findings.incidental: toggling enable_eee on port 1 caused link down plus WARNING at kernel/workqueue.c:3040 __flush_work (PID swconfig); EEE restored to 1 and link recovered; device stayed up

follow_ups: re-test with known-good cable and a different upstream switch port
try forced 100M/10M on the WAN port to test gigabit signal integrity
check whether the WAN path is meant to traverse ess-switch1's PHY rather than port 1 (ties to RT3-B005)
re-run DHCP only after RxGoodByte > 0 is observed
bugs.fix_status: EXPECTED FIXED BY R1-NET-B (same root cause) - awaiting device acceptance
bugs.r1_net_b_note: measured WITH cable on R1-NET-B; switch layer proven good in the same session
bugs.isolation_evidence: The three LAN jacks carry clean error-free traffic all the way to the CPU and serve DHCP clients, while WAN receives only corrupt frames. Same CPU, same bridge, same firmware, same session. Therefore the CPU-side receive path is healthy and the WAN fault is specific to internal switch0 port1 / eth0 / PHY7.
bugs.r1_net_c_candidate: Likely trigger: OEM dp1 declares qcom,link-poll=<1>, absent on R1. The property has NO consumer in the QDSK 5.4 tree, suggesting the 5.4 nss-dp no longer implements the OEM 4.4 link-up/speed programming. Fix may need an explicit clk_set_rate to 125 MHz rather than a DTS property alone.

probe_g_findings.oem_clocks: gmac0_rx/tx_clk_src both parent to gephy_gcc_tx at 125 MHz
probe_g_findings.hypothesis: mac_mode already 0xf -> configure skipped -> raw clock set never runs -> RCG stays xo/24MHz
probe_g_findings.register_read: NOT_MEASURABLE on OEM (no DEVMEM, regmap debugfs read fails, no 4.4 source)
probe_g_findings.next: PHASE F/G need slot switch to R1-NET-B

fix_ready.preferred: restore the vendor 125 MHz path (make adpt_mp_uniphy_mode_configure run)
fix_ready.rejected: hard-coded clk_set_rate(125000000); DTS change (DT already matches the OEM)

bugs.closure_note: RESOLVED ON HARDWARE. The recorded root_cause above is SUPERSEDED - it named the NET-C state-aliasing gate, which the R1-NET-C live install refuted (module hash verified present and running, clock tree unchanged). The authoritative root cause is: WAN is SSDK port 1 / GMAC0 / PHY-managed NON-force port, and the MP adapter bound ssdk_port_speed_clock_set() to `force_port == A_TRUE`, so GMAC0's speed clock was never programmed and the RCG stayed on xo / 24 MHz. Proven live by R1-PROBE-I (port 1: no clock setter; port 2: setter called, 125 MHz, ret=0). Fixed by R1-NET-D, which decouples speed-clock programming from the force-only gate and removes the duplicate runtime clock call.

bugs.title: Root password unset while SSH password authentication is enabled
bugs.impact: Anyone who can reach the device on the LAN - or over Wi-Fi once radios are enabled - can log in as root with no password. Remote root compromise on the local segment.
evidence: Console banner: 'There is no root password defined on this device!'
dropbear.@dropbear[0].PasswordAuth='on'
dropbear.@dropbear[0].RootPasswordAuth='on'
dropbear listening: /usr/sbin/dropbear -F -P /var/run/dropbear.1.pid -p 22 -K 300 -T 3
bugs.root_cause: Product image ships without a root password set, and does not force key-only auth.
bugs.suggested_fix_area: image defaults / firstboot flow: force password set or disable password auth

bugs.title: NSS hardware offload not provisioned - ECM module absent
bugs.impact: Hardware flow offload is the principal performance feature of this SoC. Without ECM, routing is CPU-bound rather than hardware-accelerated, so throughput on this 2-core Cortex-A7 will be far below the platform's capability.
evidence: kmod-qca-nss-ecm NOT present in opkg list-installed
/sys/kernel/debug/ecm does not exist ('No such file or directory')
ls /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/ -> only qca-nss-dp.ko, qca-nss-drv.ko, qca-nss-wifi-meshmgr.ko
xt_FLOWOFFLOAD refcount 0; /proc/net/nf_flowtable absent
no nss*/ecm* netdevices in /sys/class/net

measured_state.NSS_INITIALIZED: YES - firmware 781856 B copied to NSS core, 3 modules live, debugfs populated, DMA rings allocated

bugs.caveat: Whether ECM is intended to ship and is simply missing, or was deliberately omitted, is a design question this baseline records but does not answer.
bugs.suggested_fix_area: package selection: add kmod-qca-nss-ecm and wire up the offload path

bugs.title: board.json describes a 6-port switch (switch1) the kernel never registers; live switch is 3-port switch0
bugs.impact: The intended LAN/WAN VLAN port grouping is never applied to hardware, so VLAN separation between LAN and WAN ports is not enforced at the switch level.
evidence: swconfig list -> 'Found: switch0 - QCA MP'
/etc/board.json -> "switch": { "switch1": { ... } }
/etc/config/network -> network.@switch[0].name='switch1'
swconfig dev switch1 show -> 'Failed to connect to the switch'
swconfig dev switch0 show -> enable_vlan: 0 despite enable_vlan='1' in UCI
only ports 0,1,2 exist at runtime while board.json configures 1,2,3,4,5,6; port 6 returns '???' for all attributes
bugs.root_cause: NOT a simple rename typo. Device tree declares TWO switch instances: ess-switch@0x39c00000 (qcom,ess-switch-ipq50xx, access=local bus) and ess-switch1@1 (qcom,ess-switch-qca83xx, access=mdio). SSDK logs 'ess-switch dts node number: 2' and 'switch node is qca83xx!' but registers ONLY the first, so swconfig exposes a single 'switch0 - QCA MP' with 3 ports (cpu @ 0) and 128 vlans.
bugs.suggested_fix_area: Add the MDIO child node + switch_mac_mode, and rewrite the h3c,rt3000 board.d/02_network entry to match the OEM model.

probe_a_findings.rename_effect_measured: enable_vlan 0->1 and Port 1 pvid 0->2 (config reached hardware for the first time)
probe_a_findings.rename_limitation: swconfig dev switch0 vlan 1 set ports '2 3 4 6' -> 'Failed to set attribute: Unspecific failure'; vlan 1/2 port maps remain empty
probe_a_findings.second_switch_state: ess-switch1 present in DT but unregistered; no platform device/driver binding; only mdio device is 88000.mdio:07 (phy_id 0x004dd0c0); switch_cpu_bmp/switch_lan_bmp/switch_wan_bmp all empty

probe_b_findings.oem_model: OEM defines switch0 (internal, enable_vlan=1) and switch1 (external QCA8337, enable_vlan=0, ports '6t 2 3 4') as SEPARATE switches; LAN is a Linux bridge on eth1 and WAN is eth0 direct.
probe_b_findings.r01_error: board.d/02_network models the front panel as a single 6-port VLAN switch named switch1 and never defines the external switch.
probe_b_findings.bitmap_correction: Probe A wrongly reported the switch_*_bmp properties as empty; they are populated and correct (cpu=0x40, lan=0x1e, wan=0x00).

probe_c_findings.control_bus: mdio@88000 answered at phy 7 (0x004d/0xd0c0) - method proven
probe_c_findings.userspace_path: SIOCGMIIREG refused with EINVAL (driver has no phydev on nss-dp netdevs)
probe_c_findings.gpio26_state: undriven input reading low; DT declares it as active-high reset for ess-switch1
probe_c_findings.hw_presence: NOT PROVEN either way; chip may be held in reset, unpowered, or absent
probe_c_findings.scope_change: the external switch is not a prerequisite for basic LAN/WAN function; switch0 carries the working datapath

probe_d_findings.reset_semantics: PROVEN FROM SOURCE: assert LOW 200ms, release HIGH 10ms (SSDK qca_ar8327_gpio_reset; raw-level API)
probe_d_findings.reset_executed: YES - one pulse on global gpio 491 (pin index 26), reached deasserted/high, then freed
probe_d_findings.root_cause: CIRCULAR DEADLOCK: chip in reset cannot answer MDIO -> version unreadable -> chip_type never set to CHIP_ISISC -> reset never released. The qca83xx DT branch (ssdk_dts.c:1110) is an empty stub that sets nothing.
probe_d_findings.gpio_numbering: debugfs gpio26 is a PIN INDEX; global gpio = 491 (base 465)

bugs.title: No web management interface - LuCI not installed
bugs.impact: The only management paths are serial console and SSH. Typical consumer users have no serial adapter and expect a browser UI; the device is effectively unmanageable for them.
evidence: no uhttpd, no nginx, no rpcd process running
opkg list-installed | grep -i luci -> no results
/www/cgi-bin/ contains no usable web content

bugs.title: Wi-Fi APs default to open networks (encryption=none)
bugs.impact: Even once the radios are enabled, both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz APs would broadcast an unencrypted, open network joined to the LAN bridge. All client traffic on the air is exposed.
evidence: wireless.default_radio0.encryption='none', ssid='OpenWrt', network='lan'
wireless.default_radio1.encryption='none', ssid='OpenWrt', network='lan'
bugs.root_cause: Product image ships no default WPA2/WPA3 passphrase and no per-unit PSK provisioning flow.
bugs.suggested_fix_area: wireless defaults plus a first-boot provisioning step
bugs.conditional: Becomes user-visible the moment RT3-B001 is fixed.

bugs.title: No time synchronisation - clock stuck at image build date
bugs.impact: The system clock reads 'Mon Apr 17 13:27:22 UTC 2023', the image build time. Log timestamps, DHCP lease times, TLS certificate validation and any scheduled task are therefore wrong. Log correlation and any time-dependent security check become unreliable.
evidence: date -> 'Mon Apr 17 13:27:22 UTC 2023'
ntpd running with pool.ntp.org servers but cannot reach them
/etc/resolv.conf points at 127.0.0.1 and there are no upstream resolvers
bugs.root_cause: Consequence of RT3-B002 (no WAN). Not an independent NTP defect - ntpd is configured and running correctly.

bugs.title: No DNS resolution to the internet
bugs.impact: Clients cannot resolve external names, which is the same user-visible failure as having no internet.
evidence: /etc/resolv.conf -> nameserver 127.0.0.1, nameserver ::1
dnsmasq has no upstream resolvers because WAN has no lease
odhcpd/odhcp6c errors: 'Address not available'
bugs.root_cause: Consequence of RT3-B002 (no WAN). LAN-side DHCP/DNS service itself is correctly configured.

bugs.title: /sys/class/leds is empty - no LED support in the device tree
bugs.impact: No status indication whatsoever: no power, WAN, LAN or Wi-Fi LEDs. Users cannot tell at a glance whether the device is booting, linked or faulted. Cosmetic and diagnostic only - no routing function depends on it.
evidence: ls /sys/class/leds/ -> directory exists, exit 0, zero entries
ssdk_dt_parse_led[988]:INFO:current dts led_source_num is 0
/sys/bus/platform/drivers/leds-gpio has no bound device (only bind/unbind/uevent)
find /proc/device-tree -iname '*led*' returns nothing - no leds/gpio-leds node at all
bugs.root_cause: The running DTB contains no LED bindings. The leds-gpio driver and LED class infrastructure are present and functional but have nothing to attach to. NOT a kernel or driver defect, and NOT a permissions problem.
bugs.note: Diagnosis only. No DTS change was made, per instruction.

bugs.title: No button support - reset/WPS button not wired to userspace
bugs.impact: No input device exists for any physical button. Reset/WPS behaviour is unverified, which has recovery and serviceability implications if a user needs to reset the device.
evidence: /sys/bus/platform/drivers/gpio-keys-polled loaded but bound to no device
/proc/bus/input/devices is empty
/sys/class/input/ contains no devices
find /proc/device-tree -iname '*key*' -o -iname '*button*' returns nothing
bugs.root_cause: Same as RT3-B010 - no keys/button nodes in the running DTB.
bugs.escalation_note: Promote to P1 for serviceability if a physical reset is part of the documented recovery procedure.

bugs.title: No legitimate per-unit LAN/Wi-Fi MAC exists on this device
bugs.impact: br-lan and eth1 carry c2:3a:b8:e7:91:ef, a fallback MAC. If it is regenerated each boot the LAN MAC changes every reboot, breaking DHCP reservations and client ARP caches.
evidence: eth1 and br-lan MAC = c2:3a:b8:e7:91:ef (first octet 0xc2 has the LAA bit set)
kernel: 'GMAC2(8e890580) Invalid MAC@ - using c2:3a:b8:e7:91:ef'
U-Boot: 'eth0 MAC Address from ART is not valid', 'eth1 MAC Address from ART is not valid'
eth0 has a plausible H3C OUI: 00:11:22:33:44:55
bugs.root_cause: PROVEN. The ART partition is byte-identical to the generic Qualcomm reference caldata shipped in the firmware package: mtd13@0x1000 (1024 B) sha256 == /lib/firmware/ath11k/IPQ5018/hw1.0/caldata.bin sha256 == c2b961896eb4440ecb1a416cd77b284a9efab8d0c7dff9e2f6b2a3ed8709e499. Its MAC entries are the Qualcomm lab filler pattern (00:03:7f OUI, counter 0x123456..0x12345b). No per-unit MAC data exists anywhere on the unit.
bugs.open_question: Stability across consecutive boots is UNVERIFIED - a two-boot comparison is required.
bugs.suggested_fix_area: Manufacturing data (populate ART/ethaddr1 per unit) or a deliberately chosen deterministic derivation policy. Cannot be invented in source alone.

probe_a_findings.wan_mac_source: U-Boot env ethaddr = 00:11:22:33:44:55 (real H3C OUI, live on eth0, stable across sessions) -> LEGITIMATE
probe_a_findings.lan_mac_source: U-Boot env ethaddr1 = 00:11:22:33:44:56 -> PLACEHOLDER, kernel rejects it
other_sources_exhausted: no local-mac-address or mac-address property anywhere in /proc/device-tree
no MAC strings in mtd15 OEM rootfs
pdt_data mtd17/18 are bare UBI# headers
probe_a_findings.mac_fix_proven: PARTIAL - eth0 identity confirmed valid and stable; LAN/Wi-Fi MAC has no legitimate source

bugs.title: ART partition reads as erased on this unit
bugs.impact: Per-unit factory data (notably Ethernet MAC) appears unpopulated, which is the upstream cause of RT3-B012. Wi-Fi calibration is NOT affected.
evidence: dd if=/dev/mtd13 bs=1 count=64 -> all 0xff
U-Boot reports 'MAC Address from ART is not valid' for both eth0 and eth1
bugs.not_affected: Wi-Fi caldata comes from /lib/firmware (caldata.bin / caldata_1.bin, 131072 B each) and both phys report 'qmi caldata downloaded: type: 2'.
bugs.note: mtd13 (0:ART) is read-only in the running kernel per /proc/cmdline; no write was attempted.

bugs.title: QDSS trace config load failure produces misleading -12 error
bugs.impact: Log noise only. Two error lines per boot that look alarming ('Failed to download QDSS config to FW: -12') and could send future debugging down the wrong path.
evidence: ath11k: Direct firmware load for .../qdss_trace_config.bin failed with error -2 (three paths tried)
ath11k: qmi failed to load QDSS config: qdss_trace_config.bin
ath11k: Failed to download QDSS config to FW: -12
ls /lib/firmware/qdss_trace_config.bin -> No such file or directory; find -iname '*qdss*' -> nothing
explicitly_not: the cause of the radios being down
bugs.reasoning: -2 is ENOENT (file simply not shipped); -12 is the downstream sysfs-fallback symptom, not independent OOM evidence (MemAvailable 79188 kB, zero OOM events); both phys complete caldata download and firmware version reporting, which occur later on the same init path. QDSS is a debug trace facility and does not gate the datapath.
bugs.suggested_fix_area: ship the trace file, or suppress the fallback and log at debug level

bugs.title: Timezone defaults to UTC
bugs.impact: Logs and any time display are in UTC rather than local time, which is confusing for the target market.

/etc/TZ = UTC

no /etc/init.d/ttyd

'qcom-nandc 79b0000.qpic-nand: failed to enable serial training' and 'Serial training partition not found' at boot (no practical impact: 0 bad PEBs)
'qca-mdio 88000.mdio/90000.mdio: Could not find phy-reset-gpio' (links still come up)
'qcom-tsens 4a9000.thermal-sensor: tsens device is not enabled' yet four zones report live values
coresight-tmc/coresight-stm probe deferrals
ath11k DT coexistence params absent: qcom,pta_num, qcom,coex_mode, qcom,coex-algo, qcom,bt-active-time, qcom,bt-priority-time, qcom,pta-priority - impact UNASSESSED
bugs.note: Grouped as one polish item; each sub-item is individually harmless.

bugs.title: External QCA8337 never registers: missing phy-reset-gpio on mdio@90000 (LAN jacks dead, WAN RX dead)
bugs.impact: Plugging a PC or switch into LAN1, LAN2 or LAN3 produces no link. Those three ports provide no wired connectivity whatsoever.
evidence: LAN1/LAN2/LAN3 each measured with a real cable and live partner: PHY BMSR=0x7949 link_status=0 ANLPAR=0x0000
12s autoneg settle plus full scan of BOTH MDIO buses (8 addresses each) before each verdict
eth0/eth1 rx_packets 0->0 across 20-25s windows
mdio@90000 (external QCA8337 bus) has NO responding PHY during any insertion
swconfig dev switch1 -> 'Failed to connect to the switch' (never registered)
bugs.root_cause: ROOT CAUSE PROVEN by the OEM control experiment. The OEM DTB declares phy-reset-gpio = <&tlmm 26 0> on mdio@90000; the R1-NET-A DTB omits it. Without it the qca-mdio driver never releases the QCA8337 from reset, so the chip cannot answer MDIO (reads 0xffff), chip_ver_get() cannot identify it, chip_type is never set to CHIP_ISISC, qca_ar8327_gpio_reset() and ssdk_switch_register() never run, and SSDK reports 'no device found'. This kills the LAN PHYs AND leaves the internal switch's CPU-port forwarding unprogrammed, which is why WAN links and transmits but receives nothing.
bugs.suggested_fix_area: Bring up the external QCA8337 (DTS child node + switch_mac_mode + the chip-type deadlock), or document the LAN jacks as non-functional.

probe_r1neta_findings.next_step: physical board verification + scope on MDIO lines

bugs.fix_status: FIX BUILT AS R1-NET-B - awaiting device acceptance

fix_candidate.driver_support_confirmed: YES - mdio-qca.c qca_phy_reset() reads phy-reset-gpio; assert LOW 100ms then release HIGH 100ms; runs before of_mdiobus_register()

bugs.title: swconfig enable_eee triggers a kernel WARNING (workqueue __flush_work)
bugs.impact: Setting swconfig dev switch0 port N set enable_eee <v> raises a kernel WARNING and a call trace. No panic and no instability observed, but it indicates an SSDK workqueue lifecycle bug.
evidence: WARNING: CPU: 0 PID: 2347 at kernel/workqueue.c:3040 __flush_work+0x21c/0x220
adpt_mp_port_interface_eee_cfg_set [qca_ssdk] -> qca_ar8327_sw_set_eee [qca_ssdk] -> swconfig_set_attr
panic=0, no OOM, link and system remained healthy

bugs.title: rt3slot uses a fixed UBI image_seq as firmware identity
bugs.impact: rt3slot identifies firmware by a fixed UBI image_seq. ubiformat CHANGES image_seq on every legitimate write, so the identity is not stable across a reflash. Any slot decision or comparison built on it can be wrong for a correctly-flashed image.
evidence: rt3slot v2 (tools/rt3slot, 0e6499d4...) keys firmware identity on a fixed UBI image_seq
ubiformat rewrites image_seq as part of formatting - confirmed across every R1-NET install this project has performed
the R1-NET-C/B/D provenance work deliberately avoided using image_seq as an identity gate for exactly this reason, and used kernel/rootfs volume content hashes instead
bugs.suggested_fix_area: Replace image_seq with a stable content identity: a FIT/kernel hash, a manifest, or an equivalent content digest. Do NOT simply update the hardcoded image_seq constant.
bugs.note: Registered during network bring-up closure. Required before Product R1 ships.
bugs.fix: stable content identity in package/rt3release; tests/rb002 13 assertions; image_seq dependency removed

top_3_next_fixes.action: Enable both radios and give them a secure default
top_3_next_fixes.why: Single highest user-visible impact: with both radios disabled the device has no wireless at all, and the moment they are enabled they would be open networks. Clearing disabled='1' plus provisioning a WPA2/WPA3 PSK removes the largest functional gap and a security hole together.
top_3_next_fixes.risk: Low. Config-only change in /etc/config/wireless; no DTS, no bootloader, no partition writes. Requires a memory measurement with radios up (see unproven item) before declaring done.

top_3_next_fixes.action: Make WAN actually work - fix the switch0/switch1 naming mismatch, then confirm a DHCP lease and default route
top_3_next_fixes.why: Without a default route the device is not a router regardless of anything else. The switch naming mismatch is a concrete, reproducible config defect that also prevents the intended LAN/WAN VLAN separation from being enforced, so it is a strong suspect for the WAN jack never reaching the eth0 group.
top_3_next_fixes.risk: Low-to-moderate. Start with the board.json/UCI switch name; verify with a cable-pull port test and an upstream DHCP server before concluding.

top_3_next_fixes.action: Close the unauthenticated root exposure and add a management UI
top_3_next_fixes.why: The device currently accepts passwordless root SSH from the LAN, which is an active security exposure and easy to fix. LuCI is the other half: without it, the product is unmanageable for a normal user.
top_3_next_fixes.risk: Low for the password policy. Installing LuCI/ttyd adds packages and needs the memory-headroom measurement first, since MemTotal is only 187 MB with 79 MB available and ~47 MB of unreclaimable Slab at idle.
